summary: Same two-phase pattern with pixel-identical bar shape and colour, but the port's bar sweeps 1.8x too slowly, travels only the visible grid instead of running in/out from off-canvas, and drops the original's ~0.6 s full-black beat between phases (mean brightness 19 vs 10.7).
observations: Both sides draw the same two alternating phases on the 16x16 grid: a full-height RED vertical bar sweeping left->right, then a full-width GREEN horizontal band sweeping top->bottom, then repeat. Directions match exactly on both sides.

Bar cross-section is byte-for-byte the same on both sides: at a moment when both bars sit at the same sub-pixel position (orig t=1.8 s, port t=1.8 s) the per-column red profile is orig 0,0,0,0,0,2,17,67,161,244,238,149,59,14,2,0 and port 0,0,0,0,0,3,18,70,164,245,236,146,57,14,2,0. Lit-pixel coverage at mid-sweep is 160/256 on both.
Colour matches: peak red is (246,0,0) on both; peak green (0,253,0) orig / (0,246,0) port. meanB is 0 on both across every run - no blue anywhere.

Red bar is uniform down every row (all 16 rows read 246 at the peak column) and green band uniform across every column, on both sides - the pattern is a pure 1D function of x or of y, and the port reproduces that.

SPEED: bar centre moves linearly on BOTH sides (no easing on either). Sub-pixel kernel fit of the bar centre gives orig 0.92 px per 0.1 s = 9.2 px/s constant across the whole traverse; port 0.51 px per 0.1 s = 5.1 px/s constant. Port is 1.80x too slow. Same numbers for the green band (orig 9.2 rows/s, port 5.1 rows/s).

EXTENT: orig's red bar centre runs from x = -5.4 (fully off-canvas left) to x = +19.8 (off-canvas right) - about 1.6 grid widths of travel with ~5 px of run-in and run-out - so it slides smoothly into frame and smoothly out. Port's centre runs 0.26 -> 15.3, i.e. exactly the visible 0..15 range, so the bar POPS ON at full brightness (col-0 profile 251,225,130,47,10,1 on its very first frame) and POPS OFF at the right edge. Same story for the green band (orig -4.2 -> 19.8, port 0.0 -> 14.8).

BLACK BEATS: the original goes COMPLETELY black between phases - every pixel exactly 0 for roughly 0.6 s after the red sweep and again after the green sweep. Confirmed by a --skip 2.8 run: orig mean brightness 0 / motion 0 across the whole 1 s window while port is already showing a green band at row 0. Over a 30 s window at t=300 s the orig posts zeroMotionFrames 172/600 (28.7%) and meanBrightness min 0; the port posts zeroMotionFrames 0 and meanBrightness min 13.

PERIOD: orig full cycle 6.55 s (red sweep 0.3-2.9 s, black 3.0-3.5 s, green sweep 3.6-6.2 s, black 6.3-6.7 s), verified over 40 s and again at t=300-330 s (red phases start 301.80, 308.35, 314.95, 321.50, 328.05). Port full cycle 5.90 s (red 2.95 s + green 2.95 s, no black), red phases at 300.75, 306.65, 312.55, 318.45, 324.35. Port's cycle is ~10% short even though its bar is 1.8x slow, because it wastes no time off-canvas or dark.

BRIGHTNESS: orig mean brightness averages 10.6-10.8 over 30-60 s windows; port averages 19.0 - about 1.8x too bright integrated over time, entirely explained by the missing dark beats and missing off-canvas travel. brightnessTrend orig 'volatile' (it dips to black), port 'steady'.

PHASE TRANSITION HARSHNESS: port cuts straight from a full-brightness red bar at t=2.8 s to a full-brightness green band at t=2.9 s - motion max 26 / motionLit max 46.4 in the 30 s late window, versus orig motion max 5 / motionLit max 9.4. The original never has a discontinuity; it always fades through black.

Both sides are fps-invariant (time-based, not frame-stepped): bar centre at t=0.5/1.0/1.5/2.0 s is orig 0.31/2.63/7.15/11.71 at 10 fps, 0.25/2.24/6.70/11.27 at 20 fps, 0.21/2.05/6.47/11.04 at 40 fps - identical within one frame of grid alignment; port likewise 3.08/5.59/8.14/10.68, 2.84/5.34/7.88/10.43, 2.72/5.22/7.76/10.30. No frame-rate coupling divergence.

Both sides are resolution-independent and agree on it: re-rendered at 8x8 and at 48x48, each side's FRACTIONAL bar position at a given time is unchanged (orig 0.446 at t=1.5 s on both grids; port 0.525/0.526) and the bar half-width stays a constant fraction of the grid (~11/48, ~2/8). Neither side rasterises at native resolution.
Both sides are fully deterministic and seed-independent: dumped frames at t=1.0/1.5/4.5 s are byte-identical between seed 1 and seed 7 on both sides.
CONTROL SURFACE: meta.json reports controls: [] for BOTH sides, and --probe-controls prints '(no settable controls)' for both. No control-surface mismatch - the pattern genuinely has no dials.
Neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both), so sensor feeding is irrelevant here.
Neither side reports a compile or runtime error in any of the 14 runs.
feedback: Speed: the port's sweep is 1.8x too slow. The original's bar centre advances at a constant 9.2 pixels per second on a 16-px grid; the port's advances at 5.1 px/s. Scale the sweep rate up by ~1.8x.

Sweep extent: the original sweeps the bar centre from about -5 px (a third of a grid before the left edge) to about +20 px (a third of a grid past the right edge) - roughly 1.6 grid widths of travel per phase - so the bar visibly slides INTO frame from off-screen and slides OUT. The port maps the sweep to exactly 0..15, so the bar appears at full brightness already inside the frame and vanishes at the right edge. Extend the port's sweep range to overshoot the canvas by about one third of its width at each end (same for the green band's y sweep).

Missing dark beat: after each sweep the original holds EVERY pixel at exactly 0 for ~0.6 s before the other colour starts. The port has zero dark time - it cuts from red bar straight to green band on consecutive frames. Add the pause: the original's cycle is red sweep 2.65 s, black 0.6 s, green sweep 2.65 s, black 0.6 s.
Cycle period: with the above two fixes the total cycle should come out at 6.55 s (port currently 5.90 s). Check the period against red-phase starts spaced exactly 6.55 s apart.

Integrated brightness is the easiest regression check: the original's whole-rig mean brightness averages ~10.7 over a 30-60 s window with min 0; the port currently averages 19.0 with min 13. If the port's mean lands near 10.7 and its minimum reaches 0, the timing envelope is right.

Nothing needs changing in the spatial domain: bar profile, width, colour (pure 255,0,0 and 0,255,0), full-height/full-width orientation, sweep directions (red left->right, green top->bottom), resolution independence and fps independence all already match the original exactly. This is purely a timing/extent fix.
